resources.string: Walking and running recorded as workouts are included in steps to avoid counting them twice.
No timed activity recorded for this day.
How many reps did you complete?
Distance is estimated from today’s step count and the height in your profile.
This phone has no step-counting sensor, so the app counts none itself. Steps can still arrive from Health Connect or a connected device.

An hour counts as moved when this phone counted at least 100 steps in it — about a minute of walking, the same cadence the time above assumes. The stretch is measured from the first hour that moved, so a night’s sleep is not counted as sitting. Hours are stamped when steps are credited rather than when they were taken, so a batch the phone held back can land in a later hour and make a stretch look longer than it was.\n\nThis counts hours without walking, not time spent sitting or standing. No Android sensor can tell a seated body from an upright one, and Health Connect has no record for either, so nothing here is sent to it. A phone left on a desk counts nothing, whether you are sitting at it, standing at it or out of the room.

Without a route, time is estimated at 100 steps per minute; distance uses steps and your height. This is an assumption, not a measured cadence. Pace is distance-weighted: total moving time divided by total distance.

Completed routes contribute their moving time (excluding stops) and distance. Overlapping recordings are merged; in each hour only steps beyond the recorded distance add estimated time. Daily device totals are reconciled across the whole day.

≈ marks an estimate. Hourly totals cannot identify the exact time of each step or separate overlapping activities precisely.
Activity and estimated resting burn for the elapsed part of today.

The daily estimate uses the Mifflin–St Jeor formula and your profile: weight, height, age and sex. It estimates energy needed at rest, without walking or workouts.\n\nResting burn so far = daily estimate × minutes since midnight ÷ 1,440. Only this elapsed amount contributes to today’s total; activity is added separately. The full-day forecast is not added again. Actual expenditure may differ.

string-array.item: Step by step to your goal
Small steps go a long way

resources.string: Take it one step at a time.
If you have eaten, add the meal to your diary. If you have not, make time for a balanced meal; regular eating matters in every goal mode.
Your diary shows %1$s%% of today’s calorie target. Check for missing meals. If the record is complete, plan a balanced meal with protein, carbohydrates and vegetables.
Only %1$s%% of today’s target is recorded. Weight loss does not require going hungry: if the diary is complete, have a balanced meal and keep eating regularly.
More nourishment for your gain goal
You have recorded %1$s%% of today’s target. Check the diary, then consider another balanced meal or snack with protein. Build intake gradually, without forcing yourself to eat.
Your diary shows %1$s%% of today’s weight-loss target. Consider portions and hunger when planning your next meal. Do not compensate by fasting or skipping meals.
Your diary shows %1$s%% of today’s gain target, which already includes a surplus. Check portions and entries; there is no need to force extra food. Continue with regular balanced meals.
Your diary shows %1$s%% of today’s calorie guide. Check portions and duplicate entries. One day alone does not describe your usual diet.
A high share of fat in today’s food
About %1$s%% of recorded calories come from fat. Balance your next meals with protein, vegetables and whole grains. Fats also have a place in a varied diet; their type matters.
Saturated fat is above the daily guide
Recorded saturated fat already exceeds 10%% of today’s energy target. For the next meals, consider replacing some sources with fish, nuts or unsaturated plant oils.
Check protein for your gain goal
Recorded energy is close to your target, while protein is below half of the app’s daily guide. Consider a protein source such as beans, fish, eggs, tofu or dairy in your next meal.
